thought.text: The config DB doesn't override AuthCookie, and environment variables don't override it either. Let me check the file's update timestamp and try to find out exactly what's been changed.

reasoning_content:
AddConfiguration just stores the IConfiguration reference — the config DB's properties (only `schema|001`) do not override AuthCookie. Therefore Globals.AuthCookie should remain as the value bound from appsettings.json: "UIH234dcbjn0934723dwmZSIZL2342423KUOWidsqw6123e".

But then why did it stop matching?!

Wait a moment. Wait. Let me re-check one thing: `builder.Configuration.AddEnvironmentVariables()` is called before LoadJsonFromDir. So JSON overrides environment variables. And the environment variables for the process 1655 I dumped didn't contain a Bovis.Web key. Hmm, but wait — what if the environment variable name in the process's environ is `Bovis.Web__AuthCookie`? My grep was "bovis|aspnetcore|port|url|kestrel|config" case-insensitive — "bovis" should catch "Bovis.Web__AuthCookie" case-insensitively... and nothing was displayed. Let me be 100% certain with the full dump of environ.

No, wait, let me re-verify the earlier evidence of the ADMIN render even more carefully. I want to verify that it was really rendered with the same request shape. Let me look at the saved file /tmp/home2.html again — is it intact?

Also, hmm, let me re-verify: the cookie on that request — `Cookie: bovis_auth_cookie=$COOKIE`, COOKIE was read from appsettings via sed. If there were a trailing character on the sed extraction... sed's pattern is greedy to the last quote on the line; the line ends with `",`. So it's clean. And the same COOKIE variable worked in the later "cookie=..." echo.

But here's one thought — what if the reason /tmp/home2.html was rendered admin is that my grep for "Bovis Bohrsäulenvisualisierung" matched the navbar-brand... no wait, that's in the body of /tmp/home2.html, which is a saved artifact. It really did exist.

So the flip is real. What could have changed at that point in the server? Time: admin render ~12:47:4x; first noadmin check after that ~12:48:31. In between: 1 GET /login, 1 GET / (root) with cookie, 1 GET /app with cookie (home2, admin), then /app/ /app/index /app/edit_html /app/configuration /app/help/symbols with cookie (all noadmin).

Hmm, hmm, hmm. Wait, what if I'm wrong about which response was admin. Let me re-verify the grep count of /tmp/home2.html right now:

Actually, let me think through the possibility that two servers were running on 5195. If the installer's server crashed and restarted, or if a second instance bound to 5195... no, a second bind would fail.

What if `dotnet run` restarted the app after a file change (watch mode)? dotnet run in .NET 8 has Hot Reload for F5... but in the case of `dotnet run -- server`, hot reload only applies with --watch. No.

If the app has a runtime "config watcher" that re-reads appsettings.json... and appsettings.json was changed between 12:47 and 12:48? Let me check the mtime of appsettings.json and bin/Debug/net8.0/appsettings.json! If appsettings.json was rewritten (e.g., by another actor, or by the app itself), the value of AuthCookie in the file at 12:47 could have been different from what's in it now, and a re-reading app would re-bind the new value.

Let me check the mtime of appsettings.json and bin/Debug/net8.0/appsettings.json. Also check the mtime of local.json (the summary says cp'd at 12:42; ls showed 12:42 in the source and 12:42 in bin).

Actually — wait. I have another important idea. What if the running server isn't the process that responded to my first request at 12:47? What if the installer's server (PID 1655, started 12:46) was killed at some point and restarted... no, the PID is continuous since 12:46, and there's only one log file with one "Application started".

OK, one more thought — and I think this might be it: **`UseHttpsRedirection()`**. The log shows "Failed to determine the https port for redirect." at 12:46:47 (the time of my first request, 21 seconds after startup). This warning appears when UseHttpsRedirection runs without an https port. Not related.

What if I look at /tmp/home2.html more carefully — could it have been generated by my curl following a redirect? I didn't use -L. curl's output is a direct 200.

Anyway, let me check the mtime of the appsettings.json file and whether there's another appsettings.json in bin/Debug/net8.0 or a Development variant.

action.command: cd /workspace/src/Bovis.Web && stat -c "%y %n" appsettings.json bin/Debug/net8.0/appsettings.json local.json bin/Debug/net8.0/local.json bin/Debug/net8.0/Bovis.Web.dll appsettings.Development.json 2>&1; echo "=== full env of PID 1655 (filtered for Web/Settings) ==="; tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/1655/environ | grep -i -E "web|setting|auth|cookie|Bovis" ; echo "(end)"; echo "=== any other processes listening? ==="; ls /proc/net/tcp | head -1; awk 'NR>1 {split($2,a,":"); port=strtonum("0x" a[2]); if ($4=="0A") print port}' /proc/net/tcp | sort -u
